Internal: stop on a path holding characters R made from single backslashes

Source: R/io.R
dot-jst_check_path_chars.Rd

A Windows path typed or pasted into R with single backslashes reaches the function changed: inside quoted text R reads a backslash and the letter after it as one special character, so a backslash before t becomes a tab and one before n a new line, and the file is then reported not found under a name the user never typed (Session 343, Jeff's decision; built Session 351). An ILLEGAL escape, such as a backslash before the digit 5, stops R while it reads the line, before any function runs; that case is the guides' Troubleshooting entry, not this check's.

Usage

.jst_check_path_chars(path, what = "path")

Arguments

path

The path argument as received.

what

The noun for it in the fix line, "path" or "folder".

Value

Invisibly NULL when the path holds no control character; otherwise stops through .jst_stop().

Details

A path holding a control character (below a space, or DEL) stops here, before the file is looked for. The message quotes the path as R holds it – deparse() writes the characters back as the escapes that made them – and, when every such character is one of the seven a backslash and a letter make (bell, backspace, tab, new line, vertical tab, form feed, carriage return), gives the same path with forward slashes; otherwise the instruction alone, since an octal or hex escape cannot be told from the character it made. A path with none passes untouched: spaces, a UNC path and doubled backslashes hold no control character. Callers: jload() and jsave() on their file argument, joptions() on data.dir.
